children: Kingfisher shares rose sharply after the home-improvement retailer lifted its guidance for the fiscal year and beat analysts' profit expectations in the first half.

The company said it now expects to post adjusted pretax profit of 595 million to 635 million pounds ($795.3 million-$848.8 million) for its fiscal year compared with a previous range of 565 million to 625 million pounds.
London-listed shares rose by more than 10% in early morning trade.
"Consistent delivery, strategic progress and opportunities ahead give us the confidence to upgrade our guidance," Chief Executive Officer Thierry Garnier said.

For the first half through July 31, adjusted pretax profit came in at 404 million pounds, up 9.9% on a reported basis from the same period a year earlier, and ahead of a company-compiled consensus of 372 million pounds.
Sales rose 0.8% on a reported basis to 6.86 billion pounds, just short of analysts' expectations of 6.88 billion pounds.
Kingfisher said its results were boosted by market-share gains and momentum across trade and e-commerce. Sales at its Screwfix tools business rose 6.1% to 1.07 billion pounds.
The company also increased its free cash flow outlook to a range of 480 million to 520 million pounds from a previous range of 450 million to 510 million pounds.
